title: Pronouns and the restaurant (Unit 4 final)
description: Unit 4 check after lessons 6 and 7, with the unit's final task.

items.instruction: Fill in the gaps: The film starts at eight.
items.explanation: Review (Unit 3): anfangen splits: fängt (with ä) in second place, an at the end.

items.question: Your friend asks: 'Hast du am Freitag Zeit?' You can't. What do you say?
items.explanation: Review (Unit 3): a friendly no with leider and a reason.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: The cake is good. I'll have it.
items.text: Der Kuchen ist gut. Ich nehme ___.
items.explanation: der Kuchen is masculine: as the object, er becomes ihn.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: Will you visit us on Sunday? (informal)
items.explanation: wir becomes uns as the object.

items.question: Which sentence means 'A tea without sugar, please'?
items.explanation: ohne = without, für = for, mit = with.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: What are you having? (informal)
items.explanation: nehmen: du nimmst, with mm and no h. du bekommst is right too.

items.question: The waiter asks 'Zusammen oder getrennt?'. You're paying for your friend too. What do you say?
items.explanation: zusammen = one bill for both. getrennt = each pays their own.
Die Rechnung, bitte! or Zahlen, bitte!

items.text: Für mich die Suppe und für ihn den Salat.
items.explanation: für + accusative: für mich, für ihn. der Salat becomes den Salat.
für mich, and der Fisch becomes den Fisch.

items.instruction: Unit 4 final task. You're in a restaurant with a friend, and the waiter's lines are below. Write your reply after each line, 1-2 sentences each. Reply 1: order drinks for both of you. Reply 2: ask about the soup (Ist ...?). Reply 3: order food for both of you (für mich ..., für ihn / für sie ...); after eating, ask for the bill. Reply 4: say how you pay. Reply 5: pay, with a tip. Claude will check it. Then ask Claude for the live role-play: Claude plays the waiter.
items.prompt:
Kellner: Guten Abend! Was möchten Sie trinken?
Kellner: Und was möchten Sie essen? Heute gibt es Fisch, Suppe und Salat.
Kellner: Die Suppe? Ja, sie ist ein bisschen scharf. Was nehmen Sie?
Kellner: (später) Zusammen oder getrennt?
Kellner: Das macht zweiunddreißig Euro vierzig.
